tips.d: Lunch is 13:30–16:00 and dinner starts at 20:30, so the plan books the earliest sensible tables. Paella is a lunch dish. Kitchens close about 16:00 and 23:00.
25 Dec and 1 Jan close most shops and many sights everywhere; 26 Dec is also a holiday in Barcelona. Hotels, chains and big restaurant groups are what stays open, so book meals on those days.

Motorways are 120 km/h (less where signed) and the AP-7 has been toll-free since 2020; the only toll is the C-32 out of Barcelona airport. Old centres in Valencia, Granada, Córdoba and Seville are camera-controlled: set the satnav to car parks, never to restaurants, and give each hotel your plate number.

No right turn on a red light. On a roundabout, traffic already on it has priority, and you leave from the outer lane only. Phones hands-free only (€200 and 6 points). The alcohol limit is 0.5 g/l and there are checkpoints at Christmas, so the driver should drink nothing. Police can make a foreign driver pay a fine on the spot (half price if paid there).

Since 1 Jan 2026 Spanish cars carry a connected V-16 flashing beacon instead of warning triangles. Hazards on, beacon on the roof (from inside if you can), reflective vest on before you step out, and wait behind the barrier. Call 112 or the Sixt 24-hour number on the key tag.

The main risk in Barcelona (Aerobús, metro, La Rambla, Passeig de Gràcia), in Seville's crowds on New Year's Eve, and at the Alhambra and San Nicolás viewpoints. Keep bags zipped and in front, and phones off café tables.
Every drink at a bar comes with a free tapa, so order one round at a time.
Cards and phones work almost everywhere; carry a little cash for horchaterías and bar counters. Tipping isn't expected: round up, or 5–10% for good table service.
Spain uses Type F sockets (two round pins) at 230 V, so bring adapters for Singapore plugs.
Granada drops to near freezing at night and the Alhambra is mostly outdoors; Seville is milder but cool after dark. Pack hats, gloves and a warm layer.

Escudella and canelons in Barcelona, turrón and neules with cava, horchata with fartons in Valencia, piononos in Granada, polvorones, yemas and roscos in Seville, and chocolate con churros for breakfast anywhere.

paper.d: Singapore passport holders don't need a visa for up to 90 days in Spain and the Schengen area. Passports must be valid for 3 months after you leave and issued within the last 10 years. Carry the originals: the Alhambra and the Alcázar check them against your tickets.
The EU's Entry/Exit System registers non-EU visitors' fingerprints and a photo at the first border crossing, so passport control at Barcelona can be slow on Christmas morning.

Spain accepts a non-EU licence only with an official translation or an international permit, and the DGT advises every non-EU driver to carry one. AA Singapore issues it for S$20, in about an hour if you walk in (online takes about 10 working days). Carry it with the physical licence card and your passport.
As of 19 Oct 2026 the EU hasn't set a start date for the ETIAS travel authorisation, and it says it will announce one months ahead. Ignore websites that offer to sell one.

days.note: Land at dawn, settle into the hotel, and see the Sagrada Família while it's open (09:00–14:00 today). Christmas lunch is the main event; the evening is the lights on Passeig de Gràcia and the Gothic Quarter.

days.title: Coast road to Valencia
days.note: An early start for the coast road: about 4 hours of driving with coffee in Peñíscola, a booked paella lunch at the Malvarrosa, then Valencia's old town at sunset and the City of Arts and Sciences lit up.

stops.name: Breakfast at the hotel
stops.note: 26 Dec (Sant Esteve) is another holiday in Barcelona, so the hotel buffet is the easy choice. An early start keeps the paella lunch in Valencia on time.

stops.name: Toilet time and check out
stops.note: Taxi to T1 at 08:25 (large taxi for the cases): about 25 minutes and €37–42 (holiday rate). Ask to be dropped at arrivals and follow the 'Car rental' signs.

stops.name: Pick up the rental car at T1
stops.addr: Aeroport de Barcelona-El Prat, Terminal 1, 08820 El Prat de Llobregat
stops.note: The Sixt desk is in the T1 arrivals hall (open 24 hours, so the holiday doesn't matter); the cars are in the car park building opposite. Allow 40–60 minutes on a holiday morning: one of you queues while the others mind the bags. Each driver shows the physical licence card, the International Driving Permit and a passport; the main driver pays the deposit by credit card. Decline extras you don't need. Before you leave, check it's an automatic, the cases fit, the V-16 beacon and a reflective vest are in the car, the tank is full and whether there's a Via-T toll tag; save the 24-hour assistance number. Video the car all round.

stops.name: Comfort stop: Àrea del Baix Ebre
stops.note: About 1 h 40 from the airport and 35 minutes short of Peñíscola. Toilets, an Autogrill café and fuel, open 24 hours, on both sides of the AP-7. If you need one sooner, El Mèdol (AP-7 km 237) is 50 minutes in.

stops.name: Morning coffee in Peñíscola
stops.note: Peñíscola's walled old town sits on a rock in the sea, 10 minutes off the AP-7 at exit 43. Park in the Voramar underground car park on the Passeig Marítim, two minutes from Porto·Rico, and don't leave bags on show. The Papa Luna castle (open 10:30–17:30, €5, cards only) needs another hour, so save it. Winter café hours aren't published, so pick whichever is open. Back on the road by 12:55.

options.name: Porto·Rico Gastrobar
options.area: Seafront, Playa Norte at the foot of the old town
options.dish: All-day bar-restaurant on the promenade (menu 'for any time of day'): coffee, drinks and snacks
options.hours: Listed daily 11:00-00:00 (OpenStreetMap); winter hours not published
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): Porto·Rico is the terrace restaurant of Hotel RH Boutique Portocristo (same address and phone).
options.why: All-day seafront place with a view of the castle rock, on the walk between the car parks and the old town.

options.name: El Peñón
options.area: Old town, next to the castle
options.dish: Fresh fish and shellfish from the Peñíscola fishermen's guild; good for coffee and a light early lunch
options.price: €€ €25-40 for a meal
options.onDate: unconfirmed (checked 24 Oct): The official site gives only booking phones (964 48 07 16 / 635 53 80 97), with no hours or winter closure dates. It is an old-town restaurant, and many old-town places close in winter.
options.why: Right by the castle entrance, so it fits the castle visit.

stops.name: Paella lunch
stops.note: Paella is a lunch dish and kitchens close about 16:00, so book a 14:45 table and order the paella when you book (at least 24 hours ahead): it takes 25–45 minutes and comes by the pan, for two or more. Casa Carmela has a €50-a-head minimum and is on the way in from the north, so you can drive straight there.

options.name: Casa Carmela
options.dish: Paella valenciana (chicken and rabbit) cooked over orange-wood fire (leña de naranjo); about twenty rice dishes; the valenciana is made to order in limited numbers each day
options.price: €€€ €35-50 per person; paella valenciana for two about €50
options.hours: Lunch 13:00-16:00 (Mon-Sat); 26 Dec 2026 is not a closure day
options.onDate: open (checked 24 Oct): The restaurant's 'Calendario anual de cierres 2026' PDF (file dated 13 Oct 2026) marks December closures on 6, 8, 20 and 25 Dec and 28-31 Dec. Sat 26 Dec is not marked.
options.booking: Book now: +34 963 710 073 / +34 696 017 989, reservas@casa-carmela.com or online (valid only once confirmed). Ask for 14:45 and pre-order the wood-fired paella valenciana for 3 so it is ready; paellas are by the pan for at least 2.
options.why: The most-recommended wood-fire paella in the city, family-run since 1922, and on the way in from the north.

options.name: La Pepica
options.dish: Paella valenciana and seafood rices on the beachfront
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The official site gives Sat-Sun lunch 12:30-16:00. VisitValencia's accessibility page says it closes on weekdays in Nov-Jan and opens only at weekends, and 26 Dec is a Saturday.
options.booking: Book by phone +34 963 710 366 or the online form. Wood fire not mentioned.
options.why: A large, historic beachfront paella house (since 1898) that is easier to book than Casa Carmela; good fallback on the arrival route.

options.name: Casa Roberto
options.area: L'Eixample (Pla del Remei), about 10 min by taxi from the old town
options.dish: Paella valenciana with rabbit, chicken and snails; arroz a banda
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The official site gives only booking hours (phone 10:00-13:30). Third-party listings give Tue-Sat lunch 13:15-16:00, closed Monday.
options.booking: Phone only: +34 963 951 361 or +34 963 951 528, calls 10:00-13:30. Order the paella at least 48 h ahead; small dining room. Wood fire not stated.
options.why: A classic city-centre rice house known for a traditional paella valenciana, close to the hotel area.

options.name: Restaurante Navarro
options.area: Ciutat Vella, by Plaza del Ayuntamiento (pedestrian street)
options.dish: Paella valenciana (chicken and rabbit) and other rice dishes
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The official site says 'Cocina abierta de lunes a sábado de 13:00 a 16:00 horas', closed Sundays. Its only holiday notice is for 12 Oct.
options.booking: Book online ('Reservar mesa') or +34 963 529 623; order the paella 24 h ahead. Wood fire not stated.
options.why: Simplest logistics: park and check in first, walk to lunch, and still reach the cathedral before its 16:30 last entry.

options.name: Arrocería Maribel
options.addr: Carrer de Francisco Monleón, 5, 46012 El Palmar, València
options.area: El Palmar (Albufera), about 20-25 min by car south of the centre
options.dish: Paella valenciana, all i pebre (eel stew), arroz del senyoret; canal-side in the rice fields
options.price: €€ paella valenciana about €18 per person (blog figure); set me
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The official site gives lunch only, 12:45-16:15, closed Wednesdays except holidays, with no Christmas notice. Saturday is covered. It is in El Palmar, 20-25 min by car south of the centre.
options.booking: Book ahead by phone or through the Michelin Guide page; ask for 15:00 and pre-order the paella
options.why: Michelin Bib Gourmand (2024-2026), and its long lunch hours suit a late lunch before a sunset boat ride on the Albufera.

stops.name: Park and check in
stops.note: Through Malva-rosa and over to the Pla del Real, about 10 minutes. The Westin's underground garage is €23 a day, with a 2.20 m height limit (mind a roof box); there's no booking, and the hotel says there's normally space. The way in and out stays clear of the old town's camera zone. Then a taxi into the old town, about 8 minutes and €6–10, or a 20-minute walk through the Turia gardens.

stops.name: Miguelete tower at sunset
stops.addr: Plaça de la Reina, s/n, 46003 València
stops.note: 207 steps up the cathedral's bell tower for the sunset at 17:43 over the old town's domes; open 10:00–18:45, last entry 18:15, and 26 Dec is a normal Saturday in Valencia. Pay at the door (€3). Below it, Plaza de la Reina has a Christmas craft fair (16:30–21:00 last year), and the Tapinería Christmas market is two minutes away (weekends until 20:30). If stairs don't appeal, the Lonja de la Seda nearby is open until 19:00 (€2).

stops.name: Afternoon horchata or coffee
stops.note: Horchata (tiger-nut milk) with fartons for dunking is Valencia's own; Santa Catalina has served it since the 1800s. Winter is also chocolate season.

options.name: Horchatería Santa Catalina
options.area: Ciutat Vella, by Plaza de la Reina
options.dish: Horchata with fartons; in winter chocolate a la taza with churros or buñuelos; tiled interior (Manises ceramics)
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The official site says 'Abierto todos los días 08:15-21:30', but the page content is dated 2022. Time Out gives the same hours. No Christmas exception is posted.
options.booking: walk-in; one reviewer says cash only, so carry some
options.why: The classic old-town horchatería, around two centuries old, open all year.

options.name: Horchatería El Siglo
options.dish: Horchata and fartons, chocolate; terrace facing the Santa Caterina bell tower
options.onDate: unconfirmed (checked 24 Oct): There is no official site. One guide lists it as open daily from about 10:00 to 21:00, and an undated travel blog says it has closed. Neither could be confirmed.
options.why: Founded 1836, across the square from Santa Catalina and usually quieter.

options.name: Café de las Horas
options.area: Ciutat Vella, behind the Basilica / Plaza de la Virgen
options.dish: Coffee and cake in a neo-baroque salon; cocktails later (it is a classic spot for agua de Valencia)
options.onDate: open (checked 24 Oct): The official site (updated 22 Oct 2026) says 'Todos los días, de 10:00 a 00:00', with no holiday exceptions. Note that it closes at midnight, not 02:00 as earlier listings said.
options.why: Over-the-top baroque décor, a few steps from Plaza de la Virgen; good for a seated break.

options.name: Chocolatería Valor (Plaza de la Reina)
options.dish: Chocolate a la taza with churros, granizados; cathedral views from the terrace (no buñuelos)
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): Valor's official shop finder still lists 'Chocolatería Valor Reina-Valencia', Plaza de la Reina 20, but gives no hours. A Nov 2025 article gives Mon-Sat 09:00-21:00.
options.why: Reliable chocolate con churros right by the cathedral if the horchaterías are full.

options.name: Bertal (Plaza de la Reina)
options.dish: Horchata, pastries (bollería) and hot chocolate (no churros)
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The two sources disagree on closing time, but both cover 17:55-18:35.
options.why: Long hours on the main square; an easy fallback at any time of day.

stops.name: City of Arts and Sciences, lit up
stops.addr: Av. del Professor López Piñero, 7, 46013 València
stops.hours: Exterior walkways, pools and bridges are open…
stops.note: Calatrava's white buildings and pools are free to walk around and look best floodlit after dark, about 10 minutes by taxi from the old town. Last year a Christmas market ran here daily 11:00–23:00, with the lights on from 18:00; the 2026 programme is due in November. Then a short taxi to Ruzafa for dinner.

stops.name: Dinner in Ruzafa or the old town
stops.note: Saturday night: book ahead. Ruzafa is Valencia's liveliest food street; Tasca Ángel is a tiny standing bar famous for grilled sardines.

options.name: Canalla Bistro
options.addr: Carrer del Mestre Josep Serrano, 5, 46005 València
options.dish: Ricard Camarena's casual bistro: sharing plates mixing Valencian produce with international touches
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The official site gives no hours, and its booking runs through CoverManager. VisitValencia lists daily dinner 20:00-23:30, and Michelin lists Saturday dinner 19:30-23:00.
options.booking: Book ahead by phone +34 963 740 509 or canallabistro.com (not bookable via Michelin)
options.why: Top-chef cooking (Repsol Sol) in a relaxed room, 10 minutes' walk from Plaza del Ayuntamiento.

options.name: Vuelve Carolina
options.area: Ciutat Vella / Eixample edge, near Plaza del Ayuntamiento
options.dish: Quique Dacosta's bar-restaurant: shared plates and tapas with a Valencian base
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The official contact page (updated Mar 2026) gives Friday-Saturday dinner 20:30-00:30, with two seatings at 20:30 and 22:30 on weekends and holidays.
options.booking: Not compulsory but recommended at weekends: +34 963 218 686 or vuelvecarolina@vuelvecarolina.com
options.why: Three-Michelin-star chef's informal place, walking distance from an old-town hotel.

options.name: Memoria Gustativa
options.dish: Taberna-style cooking based on traditional Valencian recipes
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The official site (updated May 2026) gives dinners Thursday to Saturday, with the kitchen open 20:15-21:45. There is no holiday notice.
options.why: Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026, singled out in Michelin's homage to classic bars and taverns.

options.name: Bodega Casa Montaña
options.area: El Cabanyal, about 15 min by taxi from the old town
options.dish: Historic tavern: Valencian tapas, salazones, anchovies, wine from the barrels
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The official site gives no hours, and booking is via CoverManager. Both listings cover a Saturday 20:30 dinner, and no Christmas closure was found.
options.why: The city's most loved old bodega; worth the short taxi ride.

options.name: Tasca Ángel
options.area: Ciutat Vella, by the Lonja and Mercado Central
options.dish: Butterflied, grilled sardines (sardinas) bought that morning at the Mercado Central, with a beer at the bar
options.hours: Conflicting: Sat 10:30-15:00 and 19:00-23:00, or lunch only
options.onDate: unconfirmed (checked 24 Oct): Schlouk Map lists a Saturday evening service, while another guide says it opens only at midday. There is no official site.
options.why: A tiny local institution for sardines; best as a pre-dinner stop or a light dinner in the old town.

stops.name: Dessert
stops.note: Most horchaterías close by 21:30, so go somewhere open late, or have dessert where you dine.

options.name: Café de las Horas
options.dish: Cake and coffee, or a jug of agua de Valencia
options.onDate: open (checked 24 Oct): The official site (updated 22 Oct 2026) says 'Todos los días, de 10:00 a 00:00', which covers 21:40-22:10. It closes at midnight, not 02:00.
options.why: One of the few old-town cafés with cakes still open late.

options.name: Bertal (Plaza de la Reina)
options.dish: Pastries, horchata, hot chocolate
options.onDate: unconfirmed (checked 24 Oct): VisitValencia's official listing gives Friday-Saturday 09:00-21:00, which would be closed by 21:40. A March 2025 article gives Saturday 07:45-02:00. Do not rely on it for dessert.
options.why: Late Saturday hours on the cathedral square.

options.name: Horchatería Daniel (Mercado de Colón)
options.dish: Horchata with fartons; the market also has cafés and dessert stalls
options.hours: Stall hours not published; market building Sat 07:30-03:00
options.onDate: unconfirmed (checked 24 Oct): VisitValencia gives hours only for the Alboraya shop (Saturday 10:00-00:00). It says the Colón stall exists but gives no hours for it, and each business in the market sets its own.
options.why: Branch of the famous 1949 Alboraya horchatería inside a beautiful lit-up modernista market that stays open late.

drive.headline: About 4 h 10 at the wheel, 365 km, one toll (€11–13.50)
drive.total: 4 h 10 in Google's forecast, 4 h 10–5 h 10 door to door: T1 to Peñíscola 2 h 20 (2 h 00–2 h 50), Peñíscola to Valencia 1 h 40 (1 h 25–2 h 00), then 10–20 minutes across Valencia to the hotel. On top of that, allow 40–60 minutes at the Sixt desk before you drive off.
drive.route: T1, C-31 south, C-32 through the Garraf tunnels past Sitges, then the AP-7 south past Tarragona and the Ebro delta to exit 43 (Benicarló/Peñíscola) and the CV-141. After coffee, the AP-7 south past Castelló and Sagunt, then the V-21 into Valencia. On the V-21 the left lane from km 10 to 16 is a BUS-VAO car-share lane: use it only if the signs allow a car with three people.
drive.tolls: Only the C-32 leaving the airport: about €11–13.50 (the Vallcarca barrier is €8.42 at weekends and holidays, plus Cubelles). Use the lanes with the card or cash symbol, not the 'T'-only Via-T lanes. The AP-7 is free. Toll-free option: the B-23 via Molins de Rei and Martorell, about 15 minutes longer. Don't take the C-31 Garraf coast road: narrow cliff bends.
drive.fuel: The car comes full and goes back full. Today's 365 km uses about 25 litres, so no stop is needed. If you want to top up cheaply, BonÀrea at the CV-141/CV-140 junction into Peñíscola is open 24 hours.
drive.breaks: Àrea del Baix Ebre, AP-7 km 317, about 1 h 40 in (toilets, café, fuel, 24 h). Earlier: El Mèdol (km 237). Later: Benicarló (km 358), 10 minutes before the exit. On the Valencia leg: La Plana (km 445) or Sagunt (km 479.5).
drive.daylight: Sunrise 08:16, sunset 17:44 in Valencia. All driving in daylight.
drive.risks: 26 Dec is Sant Esteve, a Catalan holiday, so leaving Barcelona should be light; if the DGT repeats last year's pattern, though, Saturday 10:00–13:00 is a peak for traffic leaving the big cities. Strong north-west winds are common around the Ebro delta in winter, and there can be early fog on the coast. The Garraf tunnels and the C-31 by the airport are 80 km/h with fixed cameras. Roadworks at AP-7 km 356 (Benicarló) may still be there.
drive.check: The evening before: transit.gencat.cat for the Catalan roads, infocar.dgt.es for the AP-7 south of Catalonia, and aemet.es for wind warnings.
drive.sources: Google Maps with each departure time, ViaMichelin, Rome2rio, OSRM and Valhalla; DGT roadworks feed; fuel prices from Spain's official register. Checked 23 Oct 2026; the DGT publishes its Christmas traffic plan in mid-December.

days.title: The long drive to Granada
days.note: The longest day on the road: about 5 h 50 of driving, split by coffee in Villena, lunch in Lorca, two short comfort stops and coffee in Guadix. You reach Granada around 17:25, just before sunset.

stops.name: Breakfast at the hotel
stops.note: The Westin's buffet at Rosmarino opens at 07:00 at weekends (€28); very little else opens before 10:00 on a Sunday. Be at the door when it opens.

stops.name: Toilet time and check out
stops.note: Have the car out of the garage by 08:10 and drive off at 08:15, just before sunrise (08:20). Out over the Pont d'Aragó and Avinguda d'Ausiàs March onto the V-31, then the A-7, A-35 and A-33 to Villena, all free autovía. The long day: about 5 h 50 of driving.

stops.name: Morning coffee in Villena
stops.note: Villena sits just off the A-31 with a castle above the town, 1 h 20 from Valencia. Use the toilets here: the A-33 past Yecla has few service areas. Sunday café hours are mostly unconfirmed, so pick whichever is open.

options.name: O'hara
options.dish: Coffee, toasts (tostadas) and sandwiches
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): OpenStreetMap is the only source. It lists Tue-Thu 07:00-15:00 and 18:00-23:00, Fri 07:00-24:00, Sat 08:00-24:00 and Sun 08:00-17:00.
options.why: The one stop on this stretch with listed Sunday-morning hours; Villena adds only ~7 min to the day.

options.name: La Plazzita
options.dish: Coffee on the Plaza Mayor
options.onDate: unconfirmed (checked 24 Oct): The OpenStreetMap entry has no hours, and no other listing was found.
options.why: On Villena's main square below the castle.

options.name: Plaza Café
options.dish: Coffee and breakfast pastries
options.onDate: unconfirmed (checked 24 Oct): OpenStreetMap lists no hours, and nothing else was found.
options.why: Central Yecla, 3-5 min off the A-33 and right on the planned route.

options.name: Conca Café
options.dish: Coffee and pastries
options.onDate: unconfirmed (checked 24 Oct): OpenStreetMap lists no hours, and nothing else was found.
options.why: Next to the free car park on the same street.

stops.name: Fill up in Villena
stops.note: You must fill up today: the car has done about 485 km since Barcelona and today is about 500 km. JBM and Repsol are on the way out of town towards Yecla (about €1.74 a litre for 95 in October). If both are shut, the Galp on Avenida de Alicante 81 is open 24 hours. Self-service: note the pump number, fill up and pay in the kiosk, or pay first if the pump is locked. Petrol is 'Sin plomo 95', diesel 'Gasóleo A': check the filler flap.

stops.name: Comfort stop: Abades Sierra Espuña
stops.note: Ten minutes for toilets and a stretch, 20 minutes before Lorca. Use the southbound ('Sur') side. Repsol fuel, a cafeteria and a Burger King.

stops.name: Lorca's old town
stops.note: Park in the San Vicente underground car park (Plaza San Vicente), five minutes' walk away, then stroll round the baroque Plaza de España below the castle before lunch.

stops.name: Sunday lunch in Lorca
stops.note: Lorca keeps the drive on schedule; Murcia would get you to Granada after dark. The Parador, in the castle precinct above the square, is the one place sure to be serving on a Sunday in Christmas week, but its lunch may only start at 13:30: call it first (+34 968 406 047). If it can't seat you at 13:00, Casa Cándido in the old town (+34 968 46 69 07) is the next call. The Parador has its own car park, a 5-minute drive up from the square.

options.name: Parador Castillo de Lorca (restaurant)
options.dish: Murcian regional cooking in the castle precinct (menu not checked)
options.hours: Lunch daily (exact times not confirmed; Parador lunches usually start about 13:30); café-bar listed 11:00-23:30 (older third-party source)
options.onDate: likely open (checked 24 Oct): The parador is a year-round hotel. A Tripadvisor review dated 21 Dec 2025 mentions lunch on the arrival day, so it served lunch last December, and reviews through April 2026 show it still…
options.booking: book ahead by phone or paradores.es
options.why: Views over the Guadalentín valley, its own parking, and a reliable Sunday-lunch kitchen.

options.dish: Regional Murcian cooking (OSM cuisine: regional)
options.onDate: unconfirmed (checked 24 Oct): No hours were found in OpenStreetMap or in listings. One directory says only that it dates from 1934 and occupies a 16th-century building. Sunday lunch in Christmas week is unconfirmed.

stops.note: Ten minutes for toilets about an hour after Lorca, on the westbound side of the A-92N: a roadside restaurant and fuel. Shell Cúllar (km 377) is 20 minutes earlier if you need it sooner.

stops.name: Afternoon coffee in Guadix
stops.note: Guadix has thousands of cave houses dug into the hills; the viewpoints over the cave quarter are near the centre. Park on Avenida Medina Olmos. Leave by 16:25 so you cross the Puerto de la Mora (1,390 m) in daylight.

options.onDate: open (checked 24 Oct): The bakery's official contact page (updated 27 Jul 2026) says 'Horario: Todos los días de 7:00-22:00' for the Guadix shop at Avda. Medina Olmos 59. 27 Dec is an ordinary Sunday.
options.why: A proper bakery-café for dessert-lovers, on the main avenue with easy parking.

options.dish: Coffee by the cathedral

options.why: Closest café to the cathedral (open Sundays 15:00-18:00).

stops.name: Park and check in
stops.note: The Sercotel is just off Calle Recogidas by Puerta Real. The streets around it are behind number-plate cameras, and the satnav will happily take you through them: as a hotel guest you may drive in, but only once the hotel has registered your plate with the city, so send it on 26 Dec and ask for its exact route in from the GR-30. Granada's Christmas traffic plan can also close the Acera del Darro, next to the hotel, from 17:00 to 21:00; the hotel will know the way round. drive.headline: The long one: about 5 h 50 at the wheel, 500 km, no tolls. Fill up in Villena
drive.total: 5 h 40 in Google's forecast, 5 h 50–6 h 45 with the town ends and parking: Valencia to Villena 1 h 20 (1 h 10–1 h 35), Villena to Lorca 1 h 50 (1 h 30–2 h 05), Lorca to Guadix 1 h 40 (1 h 25–2 h 00), Guadix to Granada 50–65 minutes. The plan allows for each of these, plus two 10-minute comfort stops.
drive.route: V-31, A-7 past Alzira, A-35 past Xàtiva, then the A-33 and A-31 to Villena. From Villena, the CV-81 to Yecla, the A-33 past Jumilla and the A-30 past Cieza to Murcia, then the A-7 west to Lorca. Not via Alicante: the A-7 at Crevillent has roadworks on all lanes until 31 Dec 2026, and keep off the tolled AP-7 to Cartagena. From Lorca, the A-7 and A-91 to the A-92N past Vélez Rubio and Baza, then the A-92 over the Puerto de la Mora and the A-44/GR-30 into Granada, and the hotel's own route to Calle Párraga past the cameras. Skip the satnav's shortcut at exit 250 (Víznar/Alfacar): narrow and twisty at dusk.
drive.fuel: You must fill up today. By Villena the car has done about 485 km. Fill up on the way out of Villena towards Yecla (JBM or Repsol, 06:00–22:00, about €1.74 a litre for 95 in October). Back-ups: the 24-hour Galp on Avenida de Alicante, Villena, or the 24-hour BP at Avinguda d'Aragó 6 in Valencia, 2 minutes from the hotel on the way out.
drive.breaks: Coffee in Villena (1 h 20 in; use the toilets, as the A-33 past Yecla has few service areas). Abades Sierra Espuña, A-7 km 606, southbound side, 20 minutes before Lorca. Lunch in Lorca. Venta del Peral, A-92N km 354, an hour after Lorca. Coffee in Guadix.
drive.daylight: Sunrise 08:20 (light from 07:50); sunset 18:03 on the Puerto de la Mora and 18:04 in Granada. Leaving Guadix by 16:30 puts you over the pass at about 16:50, in daylight.
drive.risks: Frost or fog in the morning on the Altiplano (Yecla and Jumilla, 600 m) and on the Baza plateau (800–1,000 m). The Puerto de la Mora (1,390 m) is the highest point of the trip: the DGT closed it for snow on 2 Feb 2026, and black ice after sunset is the realistic risk. A right lane is closed at A-7 km 375.5–377.5 (Massalavés). Granada's Christmas traffic plan can divert traffic from 17:00 to 21:00 near the Acera del Darro. Low sun ahead on the afternoon legs: bring sunglasses.
drive.check: Saturday evening and Sunday morning: infocar.dgt.es or phone 011 for the A-92 at the Puerto de la Mora, and aemet.es for snow or fog. If the pass is closed, the DGT's detour is the A-308 from Darro via Iznalloz to the A-44 (used in Feb 2026), or wait in Guadix. Spanish rental cars carry no chains, and you need none unless the DGT declares a red level. Make sure the Sercotel has registered your plate and sent its route in.
drive.sources: Google Maps with each departure time, ViaMichelin, Rome2rio, OSRM and Valhalla; DGT roadworks feed; fuel prices from Spain's official register. Checked 23 Oct 2026; the DGT publishes its Christmas traffic plan in mid-December.

drive.headline: About 3 h 45 at the wheel, 340 km, no tolls. Car back at Santa Justa by 16:30
drive.total: 3 h 40 in Google's forecast, 3 h 40–4 h 25 realistically: Granada to Córdoba 2 h 10 (1 h 50–2 h 40) and Córdoba to Seville 1 h 30 (1 h 20–2 h 00), plus 10 minutes for roadworks into Seville. The booking ends at 17:00, so the plan has you there at 16:30.
drive.route: From the hotel to the GR-30 (ask the hotel for its exit route), then the A-92G and A-92 west past Santa Fe and Loja, the A-45 north past Lucena, and the A-4 towards Madrid to exit 401; then Ronda de los Mártires and Paseo de la Ribera to the car park. Not the N-432: it's 35 km shorter but mostly single-lane with lorries, and no faster. After lunch, the riverside road to the A-4 west, signed Sevilla, past Écija and Carmona; the A-4 becomes Avenida de Kansas City and runs to Santa Justa.
drive.fuel: Top up at the Lucena stop (Repsol, 24 h): by then the car is near the end of the tank filled in Villena. Then fill to full at the Repsol on Avenida de Kansas City (right-hand side, 06:00–22:00), 2 km before Santa Justa, and keep the receipt for the full-to-full return. Cheaper back-ups 1.5 km from the station: Petroprix, Avenida Montesierra 7, or Q8 Easy, Avenida de la Prensa 1 (both 24 h).
drive.breaks: Cred Lucena, A-45 km 51, about 1 h 30 in: toilets, a restaurant and fuel. On the way to Seville, Apolo XV at A-4 km 482 (La Campana) if you need one.
drive.daylight: Sunrise 08:27 in Granada, so you set off at first light; sunset 18:14 in Seville. All driving in daylight.
drive.risks: Morning fog in the Vega de Granada and the Guadalquivir valley (5–6 fog days in an average December) and ice near Loja at dawn: dipped headlights and a long gap, and if the DGT reports fog, accept a later Mezquita entry rather than hurrying. Commuter traffic on the GR-30 from 08:15 to 09:00. Lane closures on the last 5 km of the A-4 into Seville (km 531.9–535.3) until January. A red-light camera at the Santa Justa junction. Low sun ahead after 16:00.
drive.check: Monday evening: infocar.dgt.es or phone 011 for fog. Buy breakfast for the studio on Monday afternoon. Read the Sixt voucher for its late-return rule.
drive.sources: Google Maps with each departure time, ViaMichelin, Rome2rio, OSRM and Valhalla; DGT roadworks feed; fuel prices from Spain's official register. Checked 23 Oct 2026; the DGT publishes its Christmas traffic plan in mid-December.

actions.title: Alhambra General, Mon 28 Dec, Nasrid Palaces at 10:00
need: Full name and passport number of each of you, exactly as printed
A card that works with 3-D Secure

Add 3 adult 'General' tickets.

need: Name and passport number of each of you
Email and a password (the shop makes an account)

actions.title: Vueling VY1389, Fri 1 Jan 12:30 Seville → Barcelona
actions.cost: About €430–505 for 3 with bags (€369 base fare on 24 Oct)
need: Names exactly as in the passports
steps: Open vueling.com (English). One way, Sevilla (SVQ) → Barcelona (BCN), Friday 1 January 2027, 3 adults.
Pick VY1389, 12:30 → 14:15 (Barcelona T1). It's also sold as Iberia IB5153: book with Vueling directly.

Choose a fare with a 25 kg checked bag for each person ('Fly Grande', or 'Fly' with the checked bag), not 'Fly Light'. If a case may be over 25 kg, buy the 30 kg option now: at the airport it's €12 a kilo.
Enter the names as in the passports, pay and keep the booking code. Check in online when it opens.
If VY1389 has gone up a lot, VY1385 at 14:10 → 15:50 was the same price.
actions.note: Booked, with seats 7A–7C together and a 25 kg hold bag each. The booking code is on the flight card in Trip info. Check in online any time before the flight.

actions.title: Sixt: automatic estate or SUV, Barcelona T1 Sat 26 Dec 08:50 → Sevilla Santa Justa Tue 29 Dec 17:00
need: Main driver's details and date of birth
A credit card (not debit) in the main driver's name, used again at pick-up
steps: Open sixt.com (choose Spain), Pick-up: 'Barcelona Airport (BCN)' Terminal 1; tick 'return to a different branch': 'Sevilla Santa Justa Station'.
Filter Transmission = Automatic, Vehicle type = Estate (or SUV); open 'Details' to read the ACRISS code and luggage count.
Choose 'Pay later' if offered (flexible); choose a protection package (zero-excess if travel insurance does not cover the excess).
Add additional drivers; enter driver details and card; confirm and keep the reservation number.
actions.note: Choose 'Pay later' so you can cancel for free, and filter for Automatic and Estate (codes IWAR or SWAR) or a mid-size automatic SUV (IFAR or SFAR). Check the luggage count. Note the excess in the quote, then either take Sixt's zero-excess cover or make sure your travel insurance covers at least that amount. At pick-up, check there's a V-16 beacon and a reflective vest in the car (both legally needed since Jan 2026, and the renter is responsible), and ask whether it has a Via-T toll tag.

actions.title: Join Marriott Bonvoy (free) before booking the hotels
need: Name, email, a password and country
steps: marriott.com > 'Sign In or Join' > 'Join' > fill name, email, password, country > accept > verify email.
Then book each stay logged in so member rates and Wi-Fi apply; add the Bonvoy number to the reservation.
actions.note: Member rates are a little lower than the prices here and include Wi-Fi.

actions.title: International Driving Permit for every driver, AA Singapore
steps: Walk in to AA Centre, 2 Kung Chong Road #04-01, S159140 (Mon-Fri 09:00-18:45, Sat-Sun 09:00-17:45, closed public holidays), or AA @ GB Point, 535 Kallang Bahru #01-08, S339351, or AA @ Broadway Plaza, 4190 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6 #03-03, S569841 (both daily 11:00-19:30).

actions.title: Re-check holiday hours, strikes and New Year's Eve plans
steps: Mezquita December hours, if not booked yet.
Restaurant holiday hours on the day pages: many were unconfirmed in October.
ETIAS status on the EU site (not needed as of October).
The DGT's Christmas traffic operation (published mid-December): the peak hours for 26, 27 and 29 Dec. Move a departure 30 minutes if a peak lands on it.
Seville's New Year's Eve arrangements (sevilla.org, about 20 Dec): whether there's a public chimes event and where.
The Cathedral's New Year's Eve hours, if not booked yet.

actions.title: Install the apps
steps: Taxis: AMB Mobilitat (Barcelona), FreeNow, Cabify, TxMAD (Madrid), Pide Taxi (Granada).
Tickets: Renfe, Fever, the Sagrada Família app (tickets and audio guide).
Google Maps: download offline maps for Barcelona–Valencia, Valencia–Granada and Granada–Córdoba–Seville.

Road conditions: bookmark infocar.dgt.es and transit.gencat.cat (Catalonia); DGT incidents also show in Google Maps and Waze. Save 112, the Guardia Civil traffic line 062 and the Sixt 24-hour number in every phone.

actions.title: Online check-in for SQ388
steps: Check in on singaporeair.com or the app the moment it opens, with all three passports.
SQ387 home opens 12:35 Thu 31 Dec (Spain time).

actions.title: Print the named tickets and load the rest
steps: Print each Alhambra, Alcázar and Sagrada Família ticket on A4: they carry your names and are checked against passports.
Save every other ticket and booking to your phones: the Vueling flight, Sixt, hotels, Cathedral, Setas, flamenco, light walk, Mezquita.

actions.title: Pack the documents and kit
steps: Passports, each driver's licence card and IDP, and the credit card used for Sixt.
Type F plug adapters (two round pins).
Warm layers, hats, gloves and grippy shoes: Granada mornings are near freezing.
A small bag for New Year's Eve.
